idea-plugin.name: Interface Exception Divergence Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags a call through an interface-typed reference, wrapped in a broad silent catch (Exception e), where real implementations of that interface method actually diverge on which RuntimeException they throw directly -- a Liskov Substitution violation the static interface type alone can't warn you about: the caller was written assuming ONE implementation's behavior (e.g. "PayPalGateway never throws this"), but dependency injection can hand it any real implementation at runtime.

Built on real Class Hierarchy Analysis (CHA) -- resolves EVERY concrete implementation of the interface in the project (the same mechanism a compiler/JIT uses to decide whether a virtual call can be devirtualized), the opposite of how every other mechanism in this catalog treats "more than one real implementation" (always discarded as ambiguity elsewhere -- here it's the precondition).

Stated honestly: v0.1 only RuntimeException subtypes thrown DIRECTLY in an implementation's own override body -- never follows a call to another method to infer transitive exceptions. No PMD/SonarQube/CodeQL rule found with this exact angle; no dedicated Marketplace plugin found.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

localInspection.displayName: Silently-caught interface call diverges across real implementations
